item.title: Demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments
item.description: We have seen demands being made for people to repay loans, or purported loans, provided as part of disguised remuneration schemes. Anyone who receives a demand for repayment of a disguised remuneration loan, and is unsure whether they are liable for the amount claimed, should consider carefully whether to make any payment. Disguised remuneration schemes saw people – often contractors, consultants and agency workers – paid for their work through loans instead of regular salaries as a way to avoid tax.

item.title: More Money, Fewer Checks: These 3 Charts Show The Divide Behind VC’s Record Funding Year
item.description: One of the best ways to visualize this dichotomy is by looking at how much of the record global venture funding this year went to funding rounds across different tiers: less than $100 million, $100 million to just under $1 billion, and $1 billion and more. Our data shows that despite record venture capital spending in 2026 — nearly $680 billion through Q3 — investors are writing fewer checks to seed and early-stage companies, the businesses one typically thinks of when we talk about startups. Startup capital is both more abundant than ever this year and yet scarcer.

item.title: SafePoint seeks $100m aggregate named storm industry loss cover via Arthur Re cat bond platform
item.description: SafePoint, the expansive US primary insurer, is now seeking $100 million of annual aggregate and industry-loss index triggered named storm protection through an Arthur Re Ltd. That cat bond remains in-force until the end of 2028, but now SafePoint is looking to add more aggregate index-trigger protection to cover the risks of multi-named storm and hurricane events impacting its underwriting portfolios over the course of the coming years. For this index triggered cat bond, SafePoint is utilising the Gallagher Re operated issuance structure, Arthur Re Ltd., a platform that the broker developed to make issuance of industry-loss index trigger cat bonds more cost effective and efficient.

item.title: Global ILS expansion presents strategic capital opportunity for APAC: Howden Re
item.description: Ahead of the Singapore International Reinsurance Conference (SIRC), executives from Howden Re and Howden Capital Markets & Advisory (HCMA) emphasized that regional cedents should incorporate alternative capital into their broader toolkits to negotiate deeper partnerships and maximize optionality as reinsurers seek growth across Asia-Pacific (APAC). Dedicated reinsurance capital is now well north of US$500bn, following a period of very strong sector profitability,” commented Nena Atkinson, Associate Director, Howden Re Strategic Advisory. In a commentary published ahead of the SIRC event, Howden Re’s Andy Souter, David Flandro, Nena Atkinson, and HCMA’s Bill Cooper discussed how reinsurance capital has drastically changed shape in recent years, with institutional investors, private credit, and ILS funds now backing vehicles from catastrophe bonds and sidecars to new Lloyd’s syndicates.

item.title: PERILS finalises industry loss estimate for Australia east coast SCS at AU $1.62bn
item.description: Catastrophe data aggregator PERILS AG has published a fourth and final industry loss estimate for the Australia East Coast Severe Convective Storms (SCS) which affected the states of Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria in late October 2025, placing the insurance market loss at AU $1.62 billion, an 8% increase from the firm’s third loss estimate. Then in April, PERILS slightly lowered its insurance industry loss estimate for the event to AU $1.501 billion. Now, the final industry loss estimate for the event has increased by roughly 8% from the third loss estimate to AU $1.62 billion, PERILS has reported today.

item.title: Antares appoints Miles Robinson and Maxine Davis to claims leadership roles
item.description: Antares, a provider of insurance and reinsurance capacity, has announced the appointments of Miles Robinson and Maxine Davis to leadership roles within its claims team. In a recent LinkedIn post, Antares said, “Both appointments are a testament to Miles Robinson and Maxine Davis exceptional expertise, dedication and leadership, and recognise the significant contributions they have made to Antares. Robinson has been named Head of Claims, Antares at Lloyd’s.

item.title: RiverStone International makes ILS debut through landmark Leadenhall LPT deal
item.description: Legacy reinsurance and run-off specialist RiverStone International has participated in the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market for the first time, entering into a loss portfolio transfer (LPT) reinsurance of portfolios associated with funds managed by Leadenhall Capital Partners. The broker of record for this LPT between RiverStone International and Leadenhall Capital Partners was Aon. It demonstrates our ability to provide tailored legacy solutions across a broad range of counterparties and risk structures,” said David Rocke, Chief Executive Officer of RiverStone International Bermuda, and Group Head of M&A.

item.title: Gallagher Re names Casandra Ceballos as EVP, Facilities, Facultative
item.description: Gallagher Re, a global reinsurance brokerage and advisory business, has confirmed the appointment of Casandra Ceballos as Executive Vice President, Facilities, Facultative, with responsibility for advancing its facilities and portfolio solutions offering across international markets. In the Miami-based position, Ceballos will be responsible for shaping and expanding Gallagher Re’s global Fac Facilities and Portfolio Solutions proposition. Before joining Gallagher Re, Ceballos held the position of Vice President, Hybrid Solutions, Facultative Reinsurance for Latin America at Everest Re, where she worked within the facultative reinsurance market.

item.title: Belgian, Swedish Supermarkets Report New Suspected Freezer Hack
item.description: Several supermarkets of the ICA and Coop chains in Sweden are seeing higher temperatures in freezers, according to a report in newspaper Aftonbladet. Supermarkets in Belgium and Sweden reported sudden changes in the temperatures of their fridges and freezers on Monday, sparking fears of a cyberattack similar to those that recently occurred in France . Delhaize, which is owned by Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, confirmed that an “IT incident” took place at about 40 of its stores in Belgium on Sunday night, impacting the refrigeration systems, Belgian newswire Belga reported.

item.title: German Protests Turn Violent as Activists Clash With Police
item.description: One protestor dressed as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz became an instant selfie magnet while others called for him “to resign.” Banners read: “Eat the rich,” “We can’t feed the poor but we can fight a war?”, “your housing market is making us homeless” and “Send Merz to the frontlines.” The protests were organized by a group known as “Gen Z regelt” — loosely translated as “Gen Z sorts things out” — which had stressed in the run-up to the protest that it wouldn’t tolerate any form of violence against people or property. Mass demonstrations in Germany that passed largely peacefully on Saturday erupted in violence as night fell and rioters faced off against police in Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin. Police used water cannons to break up the crowds as protestors threw Molotov cocktails and set off fireworks.

item.title: Binance Outflows Reach $4.7 Billion After North Korea Hack
item.description: Binance restored customer withdrawals on Sunday after freezing them in the wake of the $6.4 billion exploit, which the Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed to North Korean hackers. After the hack was first detected on Thursday evening, Binance worked with industry partners, including stablecoin issuers, to swiftly freeze almost half the stolen funds. Digital asset exchange Bybit last year lost roughly $1.5 billion to an exploit that the FBI also linked to North Korea.

"PDS has built a strong business with an experienced team, differentiated technology and extensive dealer relationships," said Matt Shulman, CEO of Arch Insurance North America. and its subsidiaries, including Premier Dealer Services (PDS), a Dublin, Ohio-based provider of automotive Finance and Insurance (F&I) products and services.

item.title: Willis Re completes acquisition of BMS Re US
item.description: Willis Re has completed its acquisition of BMS Re US, including BMS Intermediaries Inc. The acquisition expands Willis Re's capabilities across property and casualty, including property catastrophe, medical malpractice, and workers' compensation. Willis Re announced the completion on 1 November 2026.

item.title: In The Car selects Earnix to support expansion into new US markets
item.description: In The Car (ITC), a provider of digitally integrated insurance programmes for automotive OEMs and dealerships, has selected Earnix's Price-It pricing and rating solution and Filing Accelerator to accelerate its expansion into new US markets. According to the release, the company will scale from two states into 18 additional markets. "As we move into more markets, we need pricing and filing capabilities that can keep pace with that ambition without adding unnecessary complexity.

item.title: Covalent Equity Partners invests in AML Analytics
item.description: Covalent Equity Partners has made a growth investment in AML Analytics, a UK-based provider of testing and validation tools for financial crime controls. Miami-based Covalent invests in technology companies with proprietary data and opportunities to expand their use of AI. Founded in 2010, AML Analytics helps regulators and financial institutions assess the effectiveness of sanctions screening and anti-money laundering systems.

item.title: Mercer Advisors completes $1.9 billion debt refinancing
item.description: Mercer Advisors has completed a $1.9 billion debt refinancing and secured a $340 million revolving credit facility, marking its first entry into the broadly syndicated loan market. Founded in 1985, Denver-based Mercer Advisors reported $111 billion in client assets as of July 31, 2026, with more than 1,730 employees and over 110 locations. Mercer said the transaction lowers financing costs, extends debt maturities and broadens its lender base.

item.title: WeRide launches insurance program with Allianz and Ping An
item.description: Autonomous driving company WeRide has launched a global insurance partnership program with Allianz Insurance Singapore and Ping An P&C Insurance as its first partners. The program will support WeRide’s international expansion, with partners developing coverage for Level 4 autonomous vehicle operations. Allianz insures WeRide’s driverless Robobus service at Singapore’s Sentosa and its Robotaxis deployed with Grab for the Ai.R autonomous shuttle service in Punggol.

item.title: Canada Life adds application status updates to AI assistant
item.description: Canada Life has expanded its AI assistant, CaLi, to let advisors check the status of pending individual insurance applications around the clock. Canada Life introduced CaLi in 2025 to help members register for workplace benefit plans. It later expanded the assistant to answer health and savings benefits questions, before opening it to advisors for process and workflow inquiries in May 2026.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re explores cyclone data backup
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance has partnered with Celest.Science to explore a backup methodology for parametric tropical cyclone insurance when key weather data is unavailable or delayed. The companies will investigate whether multiple independent data sources, combined with physical and statistical modelling, can help reconstruct a cyclone’s characteristics when traditional observations are missing. Disruptions to the data used to verify those conditions can complicate or delay payouts.

item.title: State Fund selects Stream for AI claims evidence review
item.description: California’s State Compensation Insurance Fund has selected Stream to help its workers’ compensation claims teams review medical records, correspondence, legal filings and other claims evidence. State Compensation Insurance Fund selected Stream Claims following an evaluation by its claims leadership and technology teams. Stream’s AI platform organizes documents, identifies relevant information and flags inconsistencies.

item.title: Meta Settles With Teen During Trial Testing Claims Social Media Caused Depression, Eating Disorders
item.description: The trial is the second in Los Angeles state court over claims brought by young people who say they became addicted to social media after Meta, Snap, TikTok and Alphabet’s YouTube designed their platforms to encourage compulsive use. Meta Platforms has settled with a teen plaintiff who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive, causing her mental health problems and disordered eating, attorneys for the plaintiff said on Friday. Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities alleging the companies knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing to a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression and suicide.

item.title: King Tides Flood Homes, Businesses Along Both U.S. Coasts
item.description: King tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and sending seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities in California, Florida and the Carolinas. King tides are caused by the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, moon, and sun.

item.title: Gone in 20 Minutes: How the Biggest Heist in Crypto History Unfolded
item.description: The bulk of the heist unfolded in about 20 minutes, blockchain records show, beginning shortly after 2000 GMT on Thursday. Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record digital asset theft. “In layman’s terms, the attacker may not have stolen the vault key, they may have hijacked the system that tells the vault to release money,” said Joshua Chu, a Hong Kong lawyer who works on crypto cases.

item.title: California’s Coastal Cliffs Retreating at a Rapid Rate: Study
item.description: Researchers from UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography examined high-resolution aerial lidar surveys taken in 2026 and 2023 and found that much of this coastal cliff retreat was concentrated in hotspots in Northern and Central California, and included areas retreating more than 30 feet per year. Researchers estimate 70% of the California coast is made up of coastal cliffs. The researchers findings, published in the International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation, improve the understanding of California’s coastal geology and provide a framework for systematic statewide cliff monitoring.

item.title: Brookmont’s cat bond ETF surpasses $150m AUM. GTS now lead market maker
item.description: Brookmont Capital Management has announced that the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF (ticker ILS), has surpassed $150 million in assets under management as of October 28th, 2026, which comes shortly after the fund transitioned its primary listing from the New York Stock Exchange to the Texas Stock Exchange and secured a lead market maker. In addition, Brookmont also announced that financial technology firm GTS is now the lead market maker for the catastrophe bond fund. As we explained at the time, the key drive behind this move was to expand market maker participation in the catastrophe bond fund, which proved to be a challenge when fund was first launched.

item.title: Cat bond risk spreads may decrease 10% in 2027, but market healthy and growing: Plenum
item.description: Speaking during a recent webinar, executives at Plenum Investments AG outlined that while catastrophe bond risk spreads have tightened around 15% and are expected to decrease around 10% in 2027, cat bonds remain a healthy and very diversifying and attractive asset class. Regarding risk spreads, Hopmann noted the cat bond market is currently in a softening phase. Plenum Investments recently hosted a webinar, where key executives from the firm analysed the current state of the catastrophe bond market and provided an overview of this year’s Atlantic hurricane season.

item.title: Yield normalisation, evolving risk profiles demand structural discipline in ILS: Nickerson, Icosa
item.description: As yields in ILS remain above their historical averages, and underlying risk profiles continue to evolve, maintaining market discipline requires a key focus on instrument format. Moreover, to navigate these shifting investor priorities, Nickerson noted that Icosa draws a clear distinction between what he calls Foundational ILS and Evolving ILS. According to Jordan Nickerson, Co-founder at Icosa Investments AG, navigating the year-end renewals successfully will depend on how effectively ILS managers balance pricing adjustments with contract terms and liquidity.

item.title: Everest advances commercial retail exit with sale of Chile insurance operations to AIG
item.description: These transactions form part of Everest’s strategic exit from commercial retail insurance. Upon completion of the transaction, AIG subsidiaries will acquire Everest Chile’s licensed operations, employees and ongoing insurance business. In March 2026, Everest signed a definitive agreement to sell its Canadian Retail Insurance operations, Everest Insurance Company of Canada, to The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company.

item.title: Chubb bolsters its Global Claims team
item.description: Chubb, a global property and casualty insurance company, has appointed Lisa Wilson as Head of North America Claims, Jamie Trish as Global Claims Operations Officer, and Norm Rafsol as Global Claims Technical Director, within its Global Claims team. The trio will report to Kevin Rampe, Senior Vice President, Global Claims Officer, Chubb. She has a proven track record leading teams with service and technical distinction, and I am confident her leadership will help us expand upon Chubb’s legacy of claims excellence.” Trish, in her new role, is responsible for the Global Claims operational infrastructure.

item.title: RiverStone International completes $1.6bn LPT reinsurance transactions with QBE
item.description: Global legacy acquirer RiverStone International has completed its previously announced loss portfolio transfer (LPT) agreements with QBE Insurance Group, representing approximately $1.6 billion in reserves. “Completing these transactions demonstrates RiverStone’s ability to deliver complex legacy solutions at scale. Our global platform, expertise and capital enable us to address portfolios across multiple lines and jurisdictions, creating meaningful certainty for our partners,” said Paul Brockman, Group Chief Executive Officer of RiverStone International.
